description: Central-Arabian tribal kingdom of the fifth and early sixth centuries, the first attested attempt at a unified Arab monarchy in inland Arabia. The Kindah operated as a Himyarite client at the height of South Arabian regional power and competed with the Lakhmids of al-Hira for influence across the desert. The polity dissolved after the killing of its king al-Harith ibn Amr around 528. The poet-prince Imru' al-Qais, son of Hujr the Kindite, became one of the most celebrated voices of pre-Islamic Arabic verse.

temporal.notes: Central-Arabian tribal kingdom of the fifth and early sixth centuries; collapsed after the killing of the king al-Harith ibn Amr by the Lakhmids around 528. Within atlas scope from 500 to 528.

geographic.notes: Centroid set in the Najd region of central Arabia; the polity was a confederation of mobile tribes without a single fixed capital.
